summary: A population norm exists: 18,847 Norwegian men aged 17-21 did a median of 7 strict overhand pull-ups (IQR 3-10; no kipping, full hang). So 12-15 is above the 75th percentile of young men, which makes it a reasonable 'good' target for a trained athlete. The norm comes from lighter, younger, mostly untrained men; at 95 kg the target is harder in absolute terms. The test-retest ICC was 0.95-0.96. Proposed: Keep 12-15 but relabel it as sourced: 'above the 75th percentile (10 reps) of young adult men on a strict dead-hang protocol (Aandstad 2021)'. Write the protocol into tests.yaml as dead hang, chin over bar, no kip. Possibly wrong if: reps at 95 kg plateau below 12 while weighted pull-up e1RM keeps rising (then a relative-load test would fit better).

sources.note: Aandstad 2021 (PMC8505311): men's vertical pull-ups median 7 (25-75th percentile 3-10), n=18,847; strict protocol; reported ICC 0.95-0.96.
Modified pull-up test: ICC 0.958 and minimal detectable change of 2 reps.
